newsitem.title: GHANA: Foreign firms show interest in Ghana's free zones.
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms show interest in Ghana's free zones.

text.p: Dozens of foreign companies, keen to trade with a market of more than 200 million people in West Africa, have applied to launch projects in Ghana's duty-free export processing zones, according to the head of the project.

George Aboagye, acting executive secretary of the Ghana Free Zones Board (GFBZ), told Reuters that 60 companies had applied so far and that four had been given the go-ahead to set up in the zones, which became operational last March.

The four were a South African hair care firm, a Malaysian real estate developer, a biscuit manufacturer from Lebanon and a Chinese-Ghanaian firm supplying iron rods and nails to the sub-region's expanding construction industry.

"The idea is to become a gateway to Africa, not only for goods manufactured or assembled here but also for goods in transit -- stored inside the zone and exported from here -- and for services such as offshore banking," Aboagye said.
The other applications, he added in an interview on Thursday, would be processed before the end of the year.

All companies operating inside the free zone enclaves near the seaports of Tema and Takoradi -- or as separate duty-free export processing enterprises outside the enclaves -- have to export at least 70 percent of their production or services.
Aboagye said several South African companies manufacturing consumer goods were interested in setting up sub-regional depots inside Ghana's Free Zones.
Four companies won the go-ahead on Tuesday.

Business Focus Ltd of Malaysia will build workshops for the assembly of electrical and electronic consumer goods, such as electric irons, radio and TV sets. The workshops are to be leased out to different Asian manufacturers.
Lebanese Biscuit Company (LEBISCO) plans to relocate its factory from Lebanon and expects to start production by January.
The Chinese-Ghanaian owned Great Imperial Company Ltd makes iron rods and nails.
Carson Products Company SA (PTY) Ltd of Midrand, South Africa, will manufacture its "Dark & Lovely" range of hair care products for the West African market.
Aboagye said Carson planned to employ up to 300 people and target an estimated 30 million potential women customers in Nigeria.
The total population of the West African sub-region was up to 250 million, he said, likening it to the size of the population in the United States.

Aboagye said a fish cannery, an American cosmetics firm and a Nigerian manufacturer of automobile spareparts were likely to be approved shortly. The Nigerian company planned to relocate a production unit from Nigeria, he added.

Ghana's free zones offer tax-free import of equipment and raw materials, a 10-year corporate tax abatement and 100 percent repatriation of profits, dividends and equipment. Free Zone enterprises can be wholly owned and managed by foreigners.
